manifest.description: Weather, today's schedule, up to three suggested todos, health and yesterday — written into the day's briefing note.

settings.help: A note path with {date}, or daily for the daily note.

settings.help: Latitude, longitude for the weather (Open-Meteo, no key), e.g. 51.51, -0.13. Empty: no weather.

settings.help: Adds your open items from GitHub, Linear and Jira (the note work/now).

settings.title: Prompt
settings.help: Prefilled in your language. Edit freely; the answer format is kept. Clear to restore the default.
settings.default:
Write a concise, warm morning briefing using only the supplied material. Use short paragraphs or bullets, without a heading. Keep each topic to two or three lines.
Cover, when data is available:
- Weather: morning and afternoon conditions, low/high temperatures, rain probability, and one clothing suggestion.
- Schedule: today's details and a preview of tomorrow and the following day. Say briefly when there are no events.
- Suggested todos: choose at most three realistic items from the owner's open todos, using "[Note] title". These are suggestions. Avoid pressure, overdue counts, or invented tasks. Omit when none are open.
- Health: yesterday's steps, sleep and exercise, with the three-day trend.
- Yesterday: highlights and unresolved matters.
Finish with one gentle, nonjudgmental thought for today. Omit topics without supporting data.

manifest.name: Benefit scout
manifest.description: Matches your life profile note against a catalog of Korean life-stage benefits and policy news, and publishes one weekly briefing of what is worth acting on.

settings.title: Prompt
settings.help: Prefilled in your language. Edit freely; the answer format is kept. Clear to restore the default.
settings.default:
Act as a weekly scout for benefits and policy news in Korea. Compare the supplied catalog entries and news candidates with the owner's life profile. Favor confidence over quantity: include only items worth acting on, place conditionally relevant news on the watch list, and omit irrelevant, promotional or duplicate items.
Prioritize near deadlines and the owner's current focus. For each useful catalog benefit, explain the application method, deadline and estimated amount when supplied. Clearly say that catalog information may be outdated and must be checked at the official link; never claim eligibility or verified amounts.
Write a notification-sized Markdown briefing with sections for immediate actions and items to review, omitting empty sections. Do not invent figures or facts. Watch items should explain why they may matter later and the life change that would make them relevant.

manifest.description: Each night, the day's Claude Code and Codex sessions and git history written into your daily, weekly and topic notes; new topics proposed in catchup/candidates.

settings.title: Prompt
settings.help: Prefilled in your language. Edit freely; the answer format is kept. Clear to restore the default.
settings.default:
Review Claude Code and Codex conversations on this computer for the inclusive date window supplied below. Summarize meaningful work, decisions and lessons into daily, weekly and existing topic notes; propose a new topic only when it is clearly distinct.
Probe file structures first because CLI formats vary. Read Claude Code sessions in ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl, project memory folders and ~/.claude/handoffs/latest.md. Read Codex rollouts in ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl, ~/.codex/history.jsonl and ~/.codex/memories/. Use file discovery, reading and search tools; search or chunk large logs.
Filter sidechains, tool chatter, system reminders, task notifications, hook feedback, review boilerplate and developer/reasoning instructions. Preserve meaningful user-authored content. Compare session claims with the supplied git history before describing committed work. Describe project status only from this window's sessions and git evidence, not old notes or memories. Record renames or absorbed projects in the daily; omit unsupported projects and avoid claims about long inactivity.
Put each day's work in that day's daily. Add a weekly summary only when the week has ended. Use the supplied existing topic paths to select relevant topics; do not assume a local notes mirror. Prefer concrete, durable information and reciprocal related-topic links. With many sessions, prioritize meaningful work by working directory and keep short sessions concise.

ko.settings.prompt.default:
이 컴퓨터의 Claude Code·Codex 대화를 제공된 시작일부터 종료일까지 살펴보고, 의미 있는 작업·결정·배운 점을 데일리·주간·기존 주제 노트에 남겨 주세요. 명백히 별개인 새 주제만 후보로 제안해 주세요.
CLI마다 형식이 다르므로 파일 구조부터 확인해 주세요. Claude Code는 ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl, 프로젝트 memory 폴더, ~/.claude/handoffs/latest.md를, Codex는 ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl, ~/.codex/history.jsonl, ~/.codex/memories/를 살펴보세요. 파일 찾기·읽기·검색 도구를 쓰고 큰 로그는 검색하거나 나눠 읽어 주세요.
sidechain, 도구 잡음, 시스템 알림, 작업 알림, 훅 피드백, 리뷰 보일러플레이트, developer·reasoning 지시는 걸러 주세요. 사용자가 직접 남긴 의미 있는 내용은 보존해 주세요. 실제 커밋 여부는 제공된 git 기록과 대조하고, 프로젝트 상태는 이번 기간의 세션·git 증거만으로 판단해 주세요. 옛 노트나 memory를 현재 상태처럼 옮기지 마세요. 이름 변경·흡수는 데일리에 남기고, 근거가 없는 프로젝트와 장기간 방치했다는 표현은 빼 주세요.
그날 일은 그날 데일리에, 주간 요약은 한 주가 끝났을 때만 써 주세요. 제공된 기존 주제 경로로 관련 주제를 고르고 로컬 노트 미러가 있다고 가정하지 마세요. 구체적이고 오래 참고할 정보를 우선하고 관련 주제 링크는 양방향으로 제안해 주세요. 세션이 많으면 작업 디렉터리별로 중요한 것부터, 짧은 세션은 핵심만 정리해 주세요.
